title: Go Slices vs Arrays: What’s the Difference?

scenes.say: Ever wonder when to use a slice versus an array in Go? Let’s clear that up.
Arrays have a fixed length and are value types. Slices are dynamic and act as references to arrays.

scenes.label: Capacity
scenes.sub: Slice capacity is the size of its backing array.
scenes.say: A slice’s capacity is set by the size of its underlying array. That controls how much you can append before Go moves your data.
If you append beyond a slice’s capacity, Go creates a new array. The original array stays unchanged.

scenes.question: What happens if two slices share an array?
scenes.wrong: They always see each other's changes.
scenes.right: Only until one slice is appended past capacity—then it gets a new array.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: two slices share data only until one appends past its capacity. After that, they’re independent.
